to_300.narrative: Walking the ranked list from the current 111 verified pairs: first attempt tier0 (26 leftover public-split figures inside 9 already-touched papers, conservatively estimated at 12 usable pairs after excluding 2 known-bad ones), then walk the yield-score-ranked new-paper list. The 300th pair lands inside the 42nd new paper processed after tier0 -- paper_id 17036 (DOI 10.1038/srep17803) -- with cumulative count crossing from 299 to 304 as that paper's ~5 expected pairs are added. In total: 9 tier0 papers + 42 new papers = 51 papers touched to comfortably clear 300 (a small buffer given the ~92.5% historical attempted-yield rate and the fact that expected_pairs is a rounded estimate, not a guarantee).

steps.action: leftover figures inside 9 already-touched papers -- see tier0 block

tier0.description: Public-split figures belonging to papers that already have >=1 registry.json entry (license + PDF fetch + numeric cross-check workflow already proven for these papers in design 7.39/7.43), but which were never themselves attempted. Near-zero incremental overhead (no new license check, no new PDF fetch) -- should be attempted before any new paper. Two are already known-bad from design-doc prose even though never formally logged as 'rejected' in registry.json (a data-hygiene gap worth fixing separately).

known_bad.reason: design 7.43: unit-inconsistent (raw resistivity value magnitude contradicts the paper's own uOhm-cm axis label vs. all sibling panels' consistent x1e8 conversion); already investigated and rejected in prose, just never logged to registry.json.

design 7.43: has a y-axis break (discontinuous axis) which the harness's single linear/log calibration cannot represent; already investigated and rejected in prose, just never logged to registry.json.

tier0.yield_rationale: Conservative ~50% yield (vs. the touched-paper-pool historical 76% overall / 92.5% attempted-yield) because this is deliberately picked-over remainder: the prior rounds took each paper's easiest figures first, so what's left is disproportionately the harder residue (2 of 26 already confirmed bad above; the rest include 6 untouched supplementary-info panels for paper 18869 (S6a-f) whose SI PDF may not even be in the already-fetched main-text PDF).

current_111_verified.note: core7 = {Seebeck coefficient, Electrical conductivity, ZT, Thermal conductivity, Power factor, Electrical resistivity, Lattice thermal conductivity}, the 7 quantities that already dominate the whole 603-paper corpus.

whole_corpus_ceiling.note: The ENTIRE unpaired pool (7796 curves across the 450 untouched-with-public papers) is 95.2% core7 already -- this is a domain-specific (thermoelectric materials / Starrydata) corpus, not an artifact of prior pairing choices. There is very little true diversity available to recover at any pairing strategy.

type_balance.verdict: The pure-yield-ranked plan WORSENS balance: core7 paper-presence fraction rises from 93% (baseline, 103/111 figures) to ~99% in the top-ranked new papers, because the core7_score term in the yield formula explicitly rewards already-represented quantities (as instructed) and because the corpus itself is 95% core7 in the unpaired pool -- there is very little non-core7 material to pick up even when actively looking for it. 9 non-core7-dominated candidate papers were identified (paper_ids 21387, 21395, 22107, 18779, 6211, 21297, 21560, 21710, 21733 -- Carrier concentration/Conductivity/Current/Resistance/delta-T/Open-circuit-voltage/Max-Efficiency/Voltage/Thermal-diffusivity), worth an estimated 17 pairs total, but they rank 291st-430th out of 450 by yield score (freeform figure-reference text, 1-2 series per figure, lower extraction confidence).
type_balance.fix_and_its_cost: To swap them in: drop the bottom 3 papers of the 44-paper to_300 plan (paper_ids 21357, 44933, 14602 -- together ~17 expected pairs, matching the 9 diversity papers' total) and add the 9 diversity papers instead. This keeps the final pair count at ~300 but raises the number of papers that must be license-checked and PDF-fetched from 44 to 50 (+6 papers, +14% more per-paper overhead for the same 300 pairs) since the diversity papers average under 2 pairs/paper vs. ~5.7 pairs/paper for the dropped ones. A cheaper partial fix: pull in just 21387 (6 figs, 4 expected pairs, Carrier concentration/Conductivity/Mobility) and 21395 (4 figs, 3 expected pairs, Conductivity/Current/Resistance) at ranks 291/395 without dropping anything from the top 44 -- adds 2 papers / ~7 pairs, moves core7 fraction from 99% to ~97%, reaches 300 with a small margin to spare.

caveats: Panel-level pairing viability (does the GT figure_reference actually match a single crop-able panel in the extracted image) is not knowable from the manifest -- it requires opening the actual image, exactly as design 7.42/7.43 found for papers 17037/47998 (LLM judges picked the wrong panel) and 17044 (a shared/inherited-axis panel with no tick labels of its own). The figure_reference format signal (bare/panel-lettered/freeform) used here is a *proxy* for pairing difficulty, not a guarantee -- some freeform refs will turn out fine and some panel-lettered ones will turn out to have the axis-break / shared-axis problems design 7.43/7.42 catalogued.

Broken/discontinuous y-axes (the paper 18869 Fig 3(b) case) and shared/inherited axes across sibling panels (the paper 17044 Fig 2a case) have NO field in the manifest at all -- there is no reliable proxy for either, and I did not invent one. They are only discoverable by opening the image. 'inset' is the one exception: 22 figure_reference values literally contain the word 'inset' (e.g. '6_inset', '8a inset (L)'), a genuine signal (Starrydata's own digitizer-supplied text), which I used to down-weight those entries -- but insets that aren't textually flagged this way (e.g. unlabelled insets inside a bare-numbered figure) are invisible to this survey.

License text confirmation is per-paper and NOT settled by papers.json's license_id='cc-by' field for any of the 603 papers -- that field reflects OpenAlex/publisher metadata, which design 7.32 and 7.39 both found to be wrong in both directions (paper 14482: metadata said cc-by, PDF text said NC; paper 28438: metadata said cc-by, but no CC BY text was found anywhere in the 10-page PDF and it was left in limbo, never resolved, still not in registry.json as of this survey). Paper 28438 ranks #5 in this survey's yield ranking purely on manifest signals -- flagging explicitly that it is NOT ready to pair without first resolving that outstanding HQ question from 7.39, independent of its high score.

PDF re-fetchability: NOTHING is currently on disk. data/raw/, data/cache/, data/pilot/, data/hf_dataset/, and data/eval/ are all gitignored and none exist locally right now (verified: `ls data/raw` errors, `data/cache` is empty/absent) -- this is true even for the 37 already-touched papers, so 'already fetched locally' is uniformly false across the whole corpus at this moment and was NOT used as a ranking signal. What I used instead is a manifest-level proxy: n_extracted_images>0 (179/603 papers, meaning image extraction succeeded at least once when the manifest was built) and the sparse pdf_status field (only populated for 203/603 papers per summary.json's own caveat note, and even 'ok' there is not a live guarantee -- URLs can 404/rot between manifest-build time and now).

GT-quality defects (e.g. paper 46123's all-curves-collapsed-to-x=0 case) are invisible from data/manifest/v0/curves.json, which stores only series_label/n_points/license per curve, not actual x/y values or ranges. Detecting these requires the underlying Starrydata cache (data/cache/ThermoelectricMaterials_curves.csv.gz), which is gitignored and not present locally. This survey cannot pre-screen for this failure mode at all; it is one of the 9/120 historical rejection reasons (see registry.json evidence text) and is folded only implicitly into the 0.76 historical base-yield-rate used for expected_pairs estimates.

The expected_pairs / yield_score numbers are estimates built from a small historical sample (146 figures across 37 papers, 2 rounds: design 7.39's 12-pair round and 7.43's 69-pair round) and a hand-designed scoring formula (weights: 30% figure-count-efficiency, 25% figure-reference-format quality, 20% already-represented-quantity fraction, 20% extraction-confidence, 5% series-per-figure) -- these weights are a judgment call, not fit to data, and should be treated as directional ranking guidance, not a probabilistic forecast. The 'image-not-found' failure mode (4/9 historical rejections -- a vector-drawn chart on the same PDF page as an embedded raster suppresses a page-render fallback, per design 7.21) is essentially unpredictable from the manifest.

The held_out split exclusion (464 figures / 116 papers) is this survey's own inference from the fact that all 120 current registry entries happen to be 'public' -- there is no explicit repo policy document stating held_out papers must never be paired. If HQ intends the held_out set to also eventually get verified pairs (kept secret, used only for a blind leaderboard run), that would open a materially larger and previously untouched pool -- including the 4 papers (31631, 33853, 43691, 50775) design 7.39 had already confirmed as cc-by-licensed-in-PDF but never number-checked, all of which turn out to be held_out papers. This is a policy question for HQ, not something this survey resolves on its own authority.

figure_reference free-text parsing (bare_number / panel_lettered / freeform / inset / supplementary classification) is a regex heuristic over Starrydata's own annotation text, not a verified taxonomy -- edge cases like '4a(right)', '9_upper'/'9_lower', or OCR-garbled entries ('８ ρ') were bucketed into 'freeform' by the regex even though some of these may in practice be just as easy as a clean panel-lettered reference once a human looks at the actual image.

n_extracted_images counts ALL images pulled from a paper's PDF (SEM micrographs, crystal-structure diagrams, cover banners, etc., not just chart figures), so it is an imperfect proxy for 'this paper's chart figures were successfully extracted' -- a paper could have n_extracted_images>0 purely from non-chart images while the actual line/scatter chart was the vector-drawn one PDF extraction missed (the exact failure mode behind 3 of the 9 historical rejections).
